title: U.S. House · Louisiana's 1st District
area: Southeast Louisiana, including the New Orleans suburbs of Jefferson and St. Tammany parishes and the Northshore of Lake Pontchartrain.

context.text: Louisiana's 2026 U.S. House elections use a "majority vote" (all-party) system: every candidate, regardless of party, appears on one ballot on November 3, 2026 (Louisiana's filing deadline was August 7, 2026). If no candidate wins a majority, the top two finishers advance to a December 12, 2026 general election. The partisan primary and runoff originally scheduled for May and June 2026 were canceled after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Louisiana v. Callais that the state's congressional map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, requiring a new map.

candidates.name: Steve Scalise
candidates.currentRole: U.S. House Majority Leader (since 2023); U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 1st District (since 2008)

summary.text: Steve Scalise represents Louisiana's 1st Congressional District, which runs from the Northshore of Lake Pontchartrain to the New Orleans suburbs. A former software engineer and technology-company marketing executive, he served in the Louisiana Legislature before his 2008 election to Congress. He has been in House Republican leadership since 2014 and has been House Majority Leader since January 2023.

background.text: Born in 1965 in New Orleans; his official biography describes him as a native of Jefferson Parish.
Graduated from Archbishop Rummel High School and Louisiana State University, where he earned a degree in computer science with a minor in political science.
Worked as a software engineer and as a technology company marketing executive before entering politics.
Served in the Louisiana State Legislature from 1996 to 2008, according to his official biography; Ballotpedia lists service in both the Louisiana House of Representatives and the State Senate.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2008, succeeding Bobby Jindal in the 1st District.
Served as House Majority Whip (2014-2018) and House Minority Whip (2019-2022), and was elected House Majority Leader for the 118th and 119th Congresses.

His official biography says he led the effort to pass the RESTORE Act, signed into law in 2012, which dedicated most Clean Water Act fines from the Deepwater Horizon oil spill to Gulf Coast restoration.

Critically wounded at a congressional baseball practice shooting on June 14, 2017, and returned to Congress after his recovery. According to his official biography, he and his wife, Jennifer, have two children.

priorities.text: Describes himself as focused on fiscal discipline, lower taxes, a robust national defense, strong border security and conservative values.
Says he continues working with President Trump to secure the southern border and reverse Biden administration immigration policies.
Prioritizes American energy production, saying he is fighting to enact a national energy strategy to lower prices and reduce dependence on foreign oil.

positions.summary: Says he continues to work with President Trump to secure the southern border and reverse what his site calls the prior administration's "pro-amnesty policies."
Site describes him as partnering with federal and state law enforcement to keep communities safe.
Site says he works to "give parents a say in their child's education."

record.text: Led passage of the RESTORE Act, signed into law in 2012, dedicating the majority of Clean Water Act fines from the Deepwater Horizon oil spill to Gulf Coast restoration.
Elected House Majority Leader by House Republicans for the 118th and 119th Congresses (2023–present).

summary.text: Lauren Jewett is the Democratic candidate for Louisiana's 1st Congressional District and a National Board Certified special education teacher. She describes more than 17 years teaching in Louisiana, ran unsuccessfully for the Jefferson Parish School Board in 2022 and the state Board of Elementary and Secondary Education in 2023, and campaigns on education, health care and coastal issues.

background.text: Earned a B.A. in history and political science from the University of Rochester in 2009 and an M.A. in English from Middlebury College in 2023.

Works as a special education teacher; in her 2026 Ballotpedia survey she describes more than 17 years serving students and families across Louisiana, and says she is a member of United Teachers of New Orleans.

In 2022 and 2023 survey responses, describes herself as a mentor teacher who has worked in schools in St. John the Baptist and Orleans parishes, a 2019 ASCD Emerging Leader and a 2019-2020 Understood Teacher Fellow.
Advanced to the December 2022 general election for Jefferson Parish School Board District 6 and lost to Michael Pedalino.
Ran for the Louisiana Board of Elementary and Secondary Education, District 1, in 2023 and lost to Paul Hollis, 29.0% to 71.0%; the Democratic Party of Louisiana endorsed her.

priorities.text: As a career special education teacher, says she is focused on equity for all students, mental health and wellness supports in schools, and educators' working conditions and pay, based on her prior campaign for the state Board of Elementary and Secondary Education.

summary.text: Randall Arrington is a Republican candidate for Louisiana's 1st Congressional District. A retired U.S. Navy aviator with a Ph.D. in political science, he describes careers as a naval aviator, federal law enforcement officer and university professor. He ran for the seat in 2024 and, in 2026, also sought the Republican nomination for U.S. Senate but did not appear on that primary ballot.

background.text: Born in Corona, California; graduated from Burbank High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from UCLA in 1976 and a Ph.D. from the University of New Orleans in 1999.
Served in the U.S. Navy from 1976 to 1997; in his Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as a retired naval aviator who flew attack jets from four aircraft carriers.
Describes careers as a pilot, federal law enforcement officer and university professor of political science.
Ran in the 2024 election for this seat as a Republican and received 5.0% of the vote (17,856 votes); Steve Scalise won outright.

summary.text: Liddy Glass is an unaffiliated candidate on the ballot for Louisiana's 1st Congressional District.

researchNotes: Lauren Jewett's Ballotpedia profile includes a 2026 Candidate Connection survey; her stated priorities in this guide are drawn from her 2023 BESE campaign survey. No campaign website or public statements were found for Randall Arrington or Liddy Glass beyond their names appearing on the ballot. Liddy Glass has no biographical information beyond a Ballotpedia ballot listing.
